evidence.note: Title 'About 40% of what flats on blocks C and D spend on electricity falls in daylight hours' matches costs.md (about 40% between 08:00 and 18:00, audit p6); the 'about' hedge is kept and note 2 defines daylight as 08:00-18:00.
'£612 median yearly electricity spend per flat, 2025' matches costs.md (audit p4); note 1 carries the 48 flats / 41 bills shared caveat.

Note 2 adds 'That is the share a rooftop array can supply directly', cited to the audit p6. Neither the audit claim nor pilot.md says this; pilot.md says the array feeds the landlord supply and flats get a pro-rata credit, and nowhere says the array could cover the whole daylight share.

rationale: The title and stat are faithful to the audit, with their caveats in the notes. But note 2 states as fact, under the audit citation, that the whole daylight share is what an array can supply directly. No source supports this, and it conflicts with the pilot's landlord-meter-and-credit mechanism, so it is an overclaim.
